transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-11-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Samira (Redwood Solutions), Lina (CTO, Cortexa), Marcus (Security Engineer), Daniel (Head of Platform), Priya (Legal)

Summary:
00:00 Brief intro and goals — Cortexa wants to validate Redwood for inference across regulated workloads. Primary gates: SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS/encryption story, RBAC and SSO, audit logs and retention. Evaluate hosting options: hosted API for dev, dedicated for production, private (VPC) for PII workloads.

Topics:
- Compliance status (SOC2/ISO) and evidence availability
- Identity and access (SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC)
- Encryption and key management (KMS/HSM options, BYOK)
- Audit logs, SIEM integration, log retention and formats
- Hosting modes tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
- Pilot scope and benchmark needs

Action items (summarized above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining — quick intros then we'll jump in. i'm maya from redwood, ae. ethan is our se — he'll do the infra bits. samira on solutions.
[00:12] Lina: hi, lina here, cto at cortexa. thanks, excited to explore. quick ask — we run regulated inference on customer PII, so security is first bar.
[00:20] Marcus: hey i'm marcus, security eng. i'll lead the technical security questions. we have to validate encryption, audit trails, sso, retention.
[00:27] Daniel: daniel, platform — mostly ops and deployment constraints, network egress, private links, that sort of thing.
[00:34] Maya: great. goals for today: understand where cortexa is from controls and timeline, talk Redwood hosting modes (hosted/dedicated/private), and identify gaps to sign an NDA / pilot.
[00:44] Marcus: practical constraints — we need SOC2 and ISO artifacts, evidence of KMS (BYOK preferred), RBAC with least privilege and SSO/SAML integration, and audit logs shipped to our SIEM with retention controls — legal also cares about data residency.
[01:02] Ethan: sure. quick overview — redwood has a hosted api for rapid eval, dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and a private deployment option with customer VPC and private control plane. encryption at rest and in transit is standard; we also support BYOK via KMS integrations or HSM for private deployments.
[01:24] Priya: when you say 'standard' — do you have SOC2 type II and ISO 27001? and can we get the report or an attestation?
[01:33] Maya: we do have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001, we can share a redacted report and a summary of controls. i'll send the artifacts after this call.
[01:42] Marcus: do you retain raw request payloads in hosted? our compliance requires that PII is not persisted beyond X hours unless encrypted with our keys.
[01:51] Ethan: good question — hosted stores logs for monitoring and billing; we offer TTL-based retention and the ability to disable persistent payload logging. for private deployments, logs remain in your VPC and you control retention, or we can forward logs to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk, Datadog).
[02:10] Daniel: network wise — can we do private link/privatelink type connectivity, no public egress?
[02:18] Ethan: yes for dedicated and private we support VPC peering, private link and egress controls; hosted can be restricted by VPC private endpoints depending on cloud. we'll attach a diagram.
[02:28] Lina: RBAC — we need fine-grained roles for model deployers vs reviewers vs ops. SCIM provisioning is a requirement.
[02:35] Maya: redwood supports SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with predefined roles and custom role policies. there's an audit trail for token usage per-API-key.
[02:47] Marcus: about audit logs — what fields are included? timestamps, user id, request id, model id, prompt hash, response size? format should be JSONL or NDJSON to ship to our SIEM.
[03:00] Ethan: typical audit log includes request_id, timestamp, actor (api_key or user id), model, route, token counts, errors, and optional redacted prompt hash. we can export logs in NDJSON and integrate with syslog or push to cloud storage. for hosted we also provide streaming webhook to push logs.
[03:20] Priya: retention — do you have policies for data retention and deletion on hosted instances? can we request deletion or set retention windows?
[03:29] Maya: yes, for hosted customers you can set retention windows; we also have delete-on-demand for account-level data. for production PII use cases we frequently recommend private deployments so cortexa controls retention.
[03:41] Marcus: KMS — do you support AWS KMS and GCP KMS BYOK? HSM? We have a policy that keys must be customer-managed for sensitive models.
[03:51] Ethan: yes, we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. for private/on-prem we can integrate with your HSM (nshield, cloud HSM) and do BYOK. for hosted we do envelope encryption — root keys you can manage in KMS, and we only hold ephemeral keys.
[04:08] Lina: what about attestations and access to key usage logs? we need proof of who accessed keys and when.
[04:16] Maya: in the BYOK model, key usage is visible in the customer's KMS logs (CloudTrail / Audit logs). we can also surface high-level key usage events in our audit logs.
[04:26] Daniel: service accounts and role separation — can we map platform roles to our IAM?
[04:33] Ethan: yes SCIM sync and SAML groups let you map to RBAC roles. we also support service principals that can be scoped to model endpoints.
[04:44] Marcus: are there options for field-level redaction or prompt sanitization before persist? some PII must never be logged.
[04:52] Ethan: we have a pre-ingest hook for redaction and a policy engine to drop or hash sensitive fields. for hosted we can enable automatic redaction rules; for private you can run the hook inside your network. note: redaction impacts cacheability and debugging, tradeoffs to consider.
[05:14] Priya: legal question — do you sign standard data processing agreements and support data residency clauses?
[05:22] Maya: yes we have a DPA and can add clauses for data residency in enterprise agreements. we'll share the template.
[05:30] Lina: what about incident response and breach notification SLA?
[05:35] Maya: we have an incident response playbook with 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents to enterprise customers and an escalation path. for Dedicated/Private there are tighter SLAs.
[05:46] Marcus: vulnerability management — patching frequencies and disclosure?
[05:50] Ethan: quarterly vulnerability scans, monthly patch windows for infra components, immediate patches for critical CVEs. we also provide a monthly security bulletin.
[06:03] Daniel: performance tradeoffs — if we do BYOK or redaction, does it affect latency?
[06:10] Ethan: typically small overhead for KMS calls at key rotation time; for per-request envelope decryption we keep keys cached on the runtime, so latency impact is minimal. redaction and pre-processing add CPU before request hits the model, so need to account in SLOs.
[06:28] Lina: timeline — we're hoping to run a 6-week pilot starting mid-december, must onboard legal and security in early december.
[06:36] Maya: reasonable — we can aim for a minimal hosted pilot first while we exchange docs. then move to a dedicated pilot with BYOK if that meets controls.
[06:44] Ethan: for the dedicated pilot we'll provision reserved GPU pools and configure VPC peering, plus SIEM ingestion. we'll prep a runbook and perf targets.
[06:55] Marcus: benchmarking — we want reproducible latency and token-cost numbers; can you run a small benchmark on a sample workload?
[07:02] Ethan: yes, we'll run a benchmark (seq len and prompt distribution from cortexa) on candidate models; we'll share the spreadsheet and methodology.
[07:12] Priya: contract terms — for pilot what are default liabilities and data obligations?
[07:18] Maya: we'll send a pilot agreement with standard liability clauses; enterprise agreements are negotiable.
[07:25] Daniel: do you support audit log forwarders to our SIEM over TLS with mutual auth?
[07:31] Ethan: yes, syslog/tls, or cloud-forwarders (Kinesis, Pub/Sub). mutual TLS is supported for private pipelines.
[07:42] Lina: one more — model governance and model versions. we need to pin model versions and have rollout controls.
[07:50] Maya: redwood supports model version pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models if SLOs fail. rollout events are recorded in audit logs.
[08:03] Marcus: encryption key rotation policy — how often and is rotation coordinated with us?
[08:09] Ethan: rotation is configurable; with BYOK you control rotation cadence. for envelope keys, we rotate monthly by default but can align schedules.
[08:19] Maya: ok let me recap next steps — i'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, DPA and pilot agreement. ethan will send VPC diagram and benchmark plan. we'll schedule the technical deep dive with marcus and daniel for next tuesday.
[08:33] Priya: i'll collate legal Qs and return them.
[08:36] Lina: thanks all. would be great to have a skeleton of the runbook and a list of exact log fields you can emit.
[08:42] Ethan: noted — i'll include sample NDJSON schema and retention controls.
[08:47] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and artifacts.

(End of meeting)
